claims.answer: Happy Agent runs its own loop by default and calls Claude, Codex and Grok models on existing CLI sign-ins. Optional harnesses run Claude Code itself (claude_code) and Codex CLI itself (codex_cli); Gemini runs through Antigravity and OpenCode or other ACP agents through ACP (beta). Grok is a model choice, not a separate harness. Model and effort can change mid-session without discarding the transcript. The original happy CLI wraps Claude Code and Codex directly. Happy Agent v2026.11.4 runs the Antigravity whole-agent harness through antigravity-acp@1.2.0, a community ACP adapter driving the signed-in agy CLI.

evidence.title: Happy: How Happy fits together; Original Happy CLI
evidence.locator: How Happy fits together; Original Happy CLI
evidence.finding: Happy provides Desktop for macOS, Windows and Linux; mobile iOS, Android and web; and its original happy CLI wrapping Claude Code or Codex. Desktop uses a separate Happy Agent runtime for multi-model sessions and teams.

evidence.title: Happy: Mobile access
evidence.finding: Paired phone apps continue the same encrypted sessions and allow users to read work and respond away from the desktop.

evidence.title: Happy: Supported providers; Switch models
evidence.finding: Happy runs Claude, Codex and Grok on the user's existing Claude Code, Codex or Grok CLI sign-ins, Gemini through Antigravity, and OpenCode or other ACP agents on their own login (beta). Model or effort can change mid-session without discarding the transcript.

evidence.title: Happy: Models and Subscriptions
evidence.finding: Happy uses existing Claude Code, Codex and Grok CLI sign-ins, so no Happy plan or pasted key is needed for model access; Antigravity and ACP agents use their own login. Bedrock works with an API key or the AWS credential chain.

evidence.title: Happy: Add a project
evidence.finding: Importing registers an existing folder without moving, copying or initializing Git. A project without Git uses a plain folder copy when a workspace is needed.

evidence.title: Happy: REST API
evidence.finding: Happy Agent exposes a token-authenticated REST API for sessions, streaming events and control on user infrastructure. The original happy CLI is a separate product-owned terminal entry point.

evidence.title: Happy: Skills and MCP
evidence.finding: Skills are SKILL.md files and MCP servers are mcp.toml entries, shared by every model; an agent can write both. MCP tools need Auto or Full access and every Auto call is reviewed. MCP servers from Codex or Claude Code configuration are not imported.

evidence.title: Happy: Chief of Staff
evidence.finding: The built-in Chief of Staff handles setup and task creation through ordinary conversation, including projects, remote hosts and teams. Persistent standalone issue metadata is not established.

evidence.title: Happy: Subagents
evidence.finding: Subagent trees are capped at depth three and at most five agents including finished children. Sessions have exact agent IDs for messaging and retained follow-up. This is session hierarchy, not verified issue dependency enforcement.

evidence.title: Happy: Add a project
evidence.finding: AGENTS.md files in the project tree are read by each agent and reread when they change; global AGENTS.md applies across projects.

evidence.title: Happy: Subagents; What Happy Desktop shows
evidence.finding: Subagents run in the background by default and return completion to the parent. Desktop displays subagents and running tools; tree size is bounded.

evidence.title: Happy: How agents work in another workspace
evidence.locator: How agents work in another workspace
evidence.finding: Bots and their subtasks may create a full conversation in a new workspace, with the creator as coordinator. Only the creating session may archive that workspace.

evidence.title: Happy: Subagents; How agents message each other
evidence.locator: Subagents; How agents message each other
evidence.finding: Agents delegate bounded work, choose each child model and effort, receive background completion notices and send follow-ups to finished children with retained context. Exact IDs route messages across projects or machines.

evidence.title: Happy: Durable waits and scheduled messages
evidence.finding: Primary sessions can schedule messages to known agent IDs, list or cancel them and survive intervening runtime restarts. Durable waits end early on new input. This establishes scheduled work, not an unrestricted external-event scheduler.

evidence.title: Happy: Inbox and presence
evidence.finding: Agent questions remain in the conversation and experimental Inbox; answering on one device closes the shared state. Away presence instructs agents to continue with notes instead of waiting indefinitely.

evidence.title: Happy: What Happy Desktop shows
evidence.finding: Per-session UI shows phase, tools, background processes, subagents, waiting state, whole-tree token usage and changed files. Fleet navigation has not been measured.

evidence.title: Happy: What you get
evidence.finding: The built-in Chief of Staff configures accounts, imports projects, pairs phones, deploys remote agents and creates teams through conversation.

evidence.title: Happy: Remote server
evidence.finding: Happy Agent can run on an always-on user server while Desktop connects over Tailcat and phones connect through an encrypted relay. Closing the controlling laptop does not stop work on that reachable host. Users supply host compute.

evidence.title: Happy: How Happy creates a workspace
evidence.finding: Parallel workspaces use Git worktrees on branches cut from the remote trunk. File sync and setup commands run per workspace; nongit projects use a plain copy.

evidence.title: Happy: What the OS sandbox enforces
evidence.finding: The documented OS sandbox uses macOS Seatbelt or Linux namespaces and seccomp. Shell writes, network and host sockets are restricted; file tools can still read credential folders, and MCP servers run outside the sandbox. Docker-backed sessions nest that sandbox inside the container.

evidence.title: Happy: Agents That Never Die
evidence.finding: Conversations and child sessions persist across window closure and runtime restart; finished children accept follow-ups with their full context. This is a documentation claim, not a crash test.

evidence.title: Happy: How Happy creates a workspace
evidence.finding: New workspaces copy configured sync files and run setup_commands. They start with a cold build cache. A failed setup command logs a warning while checkout and file sync determine readiness.

evidence.title: Happy: Use several accounts; Provider usage and quotas
evidence.locator: Use several accounts; Provider usage and quotas
evidence.finding: Smart provider pools can rotate same-provider accounts after authentication or quota-exhaustion errors. Provider quotas are polled about every fifteen minutes and are observations rather than billing records.

evidence.title: Happy: What Happy Desktop shows
evidence.finding: Session status includes active tools, background work, subagents, waiting state, tokens and changed files. Deliberate failure and approval consistency after reconnect remain untested.

evidence.title: Happy: Provider usage and quotas
evidence.finding: Provider quotas are polled about every fifteen minutes and shown in the app; they are observations, not billing records.

evidence.title: Happy: Shared work
evidence.finding: Team members see the same projects and sessions and can speak to the agent. Changes in speaker include the member name/email; per-member drafts and task ordering stay personal.

evidence.title: Happy: Owner; Sign-in; Leaving
evidence.finding: Team mode verifies per-user WorkOS tokens. The owner alone renames the installation, toggles global skills or archives others tasks; members otherwise have equal access and can select Full access. A remove-member action is explicitly not built yet.

evidence.title: Happy: Four permission modes; Auto review
evidence.finding: Read only, Workspace write, Auto and Full access share a permission model. Auto sends boundary-crossing actions to a separate read-only reviewer and grants only that execution if allowed. Reads and workspace edits are not reviewed.

evidence.title: Happy: Switch models; How compaction works
evidence.finding: Session transcripts retain provider-specific opaque data; compaction creates a visible message describing replaced content. No immutable audit retention guarantee was verified.

evidence.title: Happy: Initial core release; Current interface
evidence.finding: The desktop interface has conversations, files, diffs and an attachable terminal; current docs describe changed files beside each conversation. Guided batch review was not established.

evidence.title: Happy: Shared work
evidence.finding: Named teammates operate on shared sessions and projects on the same team server. This is not a verified transfer preserving every permission and runtime detail after owner disconnect.

evidence.title: Happy: Artifacts
evidence.finding: The Chief of Staff documentation links a recipe for building a live, shared HTML artifact. No exact-revision cross-task gallery test was run.

evidence.title: Happy: MIT License
evidence.finding: The mobile app, original CLI and relay repository has the MIT license. Happy Desktop documentation also explicitly describes its app/runtime as MIT. Hosted and provider services remain separate.

evidence.title: Happy: How a Happy team server works
evidence.locator: How a Happy team server works
evidence.finding: The core Happy Agent runs self-hosted on user machines or servers, with Desktop connecting remotely. Happy Social/WorkOS team sign-in and the mobile relay are distinct service dependencies.

evidence.title: Happy: Analytics: PostHog
evidence.finding: Happy apps send pseudonymous product usage events to PostHog, excluding message content, prompts, code and file names, and offer a Settings opt-out that stops them; the desktop app has its own switch. Happy Agent itself sends no analytics.

evidence.title: Happy: What does Happy cost?
evidence.finding: Happy is free and MIT licensed. Model use is paid through existing subscriptions and user compute. Phone voice has twenty free minutes per thirty days and an optional paid allowance; custom ElevenLabs use is separate.

evidence.title: Happy: October 26, 2026
evidence.finding: Happy Agent v0.4.108 adds GPT-6.1 Terra and stop-state persistence; Desktop v0.0.102 has opt-in beta Stem cells. Current release activity does not imply all experimental UI is enabled by default.

evidence.title: Happy: What does Happy cost?
evidence.finding: The desktop application and self-hosted runtime are free. Model subscriptions and host compute are separate costs; optional phone voice has its own allowance.

evidence.title: Happy: What does Happy cost?
evidence.finding: The core ADE has no software subscription charge; coding-model subscriptions, host resources and optional voice are separately scoped. No standardized task-scenario total was invented.

evidence.title: Happy: Harnesses: Claude Code, Codex CLI, Antigravity, OpenCode, and ACP agents
evidence.finding: Happy's own harness runs the loop by default; the claude_code harness runs Claude Code itself on a claude account and codex_cli does the same for Codex, while Antigravity, OpenCode and other ACP agents sign in themselves. Grok is not listed as a harness.

evidence.title: Happy website source: Set up enterprise JWT sign-in
evidence.finding: Recipe for a team-mode Happy Agent whose members sign in through the organization's own identity provider (Okta, Entra ID, Google Workspace, Keycloak or internal SSO) instead of Happy's WorkOS accounts; the daemon verifies JWTs from an organization-owned OAuth authorization server and needs an Agent release with enterprise JWT authentication.

evidence.title: Happy Agent TeamJwtConfig at release v2026.11.4
evidence.finding: The released Happy Agent v2026.11.4 parses a [feature.team.jwt] machine configuration with an authorization URL and exactly one of a JWKS URL, public key or secret, used to verify organization-issued team tokens.

evidence.title: Happy Desktop server sign-in discovery at release v0.0.103
evidence.finding: The released desktop app v0.0.103 queries a Happy Agent server's v0/authentication endpoint to discover its sign-in methods.

evidence.title: Happy Antigravity support at v2026.11.4
evidence.finding: Happy Agent v2026.11.4 runs the Antigravity whole-agent harness through antigravity-acp@1.2.0, a community ACP adapter driving the signed-in agy CLI.
